title: 21st Sitting of second session of 2025
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Fonadhoo); Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim (Dhiggaru) presided after the recess (he also spoke once as a member in item 6.1)
summary: The sitting opened at 09:03 with 29 members present, 7 on leave and 2 on official travel, and the first reading of a Tax Administration Act amendment bill was announced. Members then held the preliminary debate on a government bill amending the National Payment System Act so the Monetary Authority can set up entities to run payment systems: supporters said it would cut costs and money lost in transfers, while critics argued a regulator should not run businesses and questioned the central bank's record. Dr Ahmed Shamheed's resolution seeking the same electricity and water prices for small and medium businesses outside Malé was debated, and after the recess a Penal Code amendment drew no speakers and a Water and Sewerage Act amendment (extending a deadline for building the systems) was still being debated when this part ends. No votes were recorded in this part. This part finishes the debate on a government bill to amend the Water and Sewerage Act, which sets 2027 as the deadline for water and sewerage systems on every inhabited island. Members from several islands described unfinished or failed systems and said they back the bill, and the sponsor closed the debate. Members then heard and debated the Judiciary Committee's report on the President's nominee for the Supreme Court. After a recess, the Majlis voted on five matters: it accepted the water and sewerage bill, a payment-system bill, a Penal Code bill and a resolution on power and water costs for small businesses for committee study, and approved the Supreme Court nominee 62-0.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Opposed the bill, arguing a regulator like the central bank should not set up companies to do business.
Criticised the central bank over the dollar black market, lost funds and high bank lending rates.
Said committee sessions with the central bank governor should not be kept secret from the public.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: On the payment bill, asked whether the Monetary Authority should form a company itself, and cited its revised growth figures and reserves.
Raised a point of order saying the statistics he quoted had been published by the Monetary Authority and were not secret.
On his resolution, said it is non-partisan and cited a MVR 138 million STELCO profit and price gaps between Malé and atolls.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said businesses in atolls pay far more per unit of power and water and asked for rates equal to Greater Malé.
Said Velidhoo still lacks adequate voltage, and criticised the opposition's record on the issue.
Supported the amendments and said he hopes every inhabited island will have water and sewerage by 2027.
Said unfinished sewerage works in Lhohi (in his constituency) should be completed so that residents get the service.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said past government agreements and losses, such as an audit finding on RDC documents, make cheap services hard to deliver.
Said utility bills sent to old phone numbers leave landlords liable and called for a better billing system.
Said electricity prices were most recently lowered by the current government.

speakers.name: Adam Shafeeq
positions: Said the Payment System Act amendment lets the Monetary Authority create entities to run national payment systems, reducing reliance on outside operators.
In closing, said the changes would help online, retail and other businesses and asked the committee to refine the bill.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Supported the amendment, saying a national payment gateway linked to local and international banks would cut costs for businesses.
Raised a point of order saying the Hanimaadhoo member's claims about other countries were inaccurate.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Supported the bill, saying a national payment system would curb money lost in digital transfers and scams.
Supported the amendment, noting that a 2025 target in the law was missed and the new deadline is 2027.
Said the systems must be designed with each island's future growth in mind and that councils should be involved.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Backed the payment amendments, saying the points raised against them were not a concern from the nation's viewpoint.
Said the governor did not answer committee questions on the effect of the proposed foreign-currency change.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Supported the resolution, saying services such as electricity and water should be provided on an equal basis across the country.
As the bill's sponsor, closed the debate and thanked members who spoke.
Said many islands have sewerage or water works that were started but not finished, and the amendment aims to get them done by 2027.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said atoll residents complain mainly because services are missing, citing a delayed water and sewerage project in Nellaidhoo.
Raised a point of order during the Mathiveri member's speech.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Supported the resolution, saying essential services should be affordable and that wastage and corruption raise costs.
Thanked the bill's sponsor and said the government is acting on its manifesto promise on water and sewerage.
Argued that earlier governments failed to deliver the services, citing debts and unfinished works.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Supported the bill and described Manadhoo's sewerage system as unrepaired since 2014, causing blockages and damage to homes.
Criticised how previous governments handled water and sewerage projects and said the 2027 deadline is credible.
Presented the Judiciary Committee's report on the Supreme Court nominee, including what the committee checked.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the amendment as a way to bring proven international payment practices in, with details refined at committee stage.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the bill as important for digital payments and asked that it pass quickly through committee.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Supported the resolution, saying energy and water make up a large share of small business costs and some incentive is needed.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Supported extending the water and sewerage deadline, saying earlier projects were wasteful and handed to unsuitable contractors.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Supported the bill, saying water and sewerage are core services long promised and the government aims to deliver them to all islands.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Supported extending the deadline, but asked the committee to clarify the penalty for misusing the water system.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shameez
positions: Said new sewerage systems in his constituency's islands have caused serious problems and asked why the work went to companies without experience.
Called on the government to finish the water and sewerage works in Madaveli and Nadellaa quickly.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Supported the bill and criticised how the previous MDP government awarded and funded water and sewerage projects.
Said many sewerage projects were started before the 2023 presidential election and left unfinished.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: For the PNC, supported the Judiciary Committee's report and said the nominee is a capable, honest person with court experience.

decisions: Chair announced PNC committee changes: Ihavandhoo member Ahmed Naseer replaces Baarashu member Ibrahim Shujau on the State Owned Enterprises Committee, and Vilifushi member Hassan Waheed replaces Huraa member Dr. Anara Naeem on the Judiciary Committee.
Chair reminded members not to repeat in the chamber what was said in closed committee meetings.
Preliminary debate on the Payment System Act amendment bill concluded; vote on accepting it set for the day's voting time.
Debate on Dr Ahmed Shamheed's resolution on electricity and water prices concluded.
Debate on the Penal Code amendment bill closed with no speakers; vote at the day's voting time.
The bill to amend the Water and Sewerage Act (2020/8), sponsored by Abdul Latheef Mohamed, was accepted for consideration and sent to the Environment and Climate Change Committee.
A bill by Adam Shafeeq (Makunudhoo) to amend the National Payment System Act (2021/8) was accepted and sent to the Finance Committee.
A resolution by Dr. Ahmed Shamheed on power and water costs for small and medium businesses outside Malé was accepted and sent to the Environment and Climate Change Committee.
A bill by Meekail Ahmed Nasym (South Galolhu) to amend the Penal Code (2014/9) was accepted and sent to the Judiciary Committee.
The Majlis approved the appointment of Abdulghani Mohamed (H. Hostside) as a Supreme Court Justice, 62-0.
The next sitting was set for Wednesday 6 August 2025 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accept Adam Shafeeq's bill to amend the National Payment System Act (2021/8) for consideration
Accept Dr. Ahmed Shamheed's resolution on power and water costs for small and medium businesses outside Malé
Accept Meekail Ahmed Nasym's bill to amend the Penal Code (2014/9) for consideration
Accept the bill to amend the Water and Sewerage Act (2020/8) for consideration
Approve Abdulghani Mohamed as Supreme Court Justice (Judiciary Committee report)
